paragraphs.text: **Measured:** of the three settings, collaborative tuition ran furthest over budget: $776,088 across 6 of 17 years. Private schools ran $510,256 over in their bad years; Lunenburg’s own schools, $258,209.

**Two things sit beside it.** The collaborative line has had almost no slack: $56,598 over on balance across those years, where private ran $1,409,774 under. And a child arriving already in a collaborative is Lunenburg’s from the first day, with no year paid by the old town (our reading of c.71B §5).
**Not shown:** whether either of those caused the overruns, or how many children did. That needs counts the district does not publish: the Surprise costs page names them.

views.note: An example, not any child’s bill: $230,514 a year, the average private placement, FY2022 to FY2025 (private tuition divided by the children placed, our estimate), split by the months left in the school year. The law: the town the child came from pays the rest of that year; from 1 April to 30 June, the next year too. A child placed here who was not already placed is Lunenburg’s from the start. If the new team changes the placement, Lunenburg pays any increase. A year later the state repays about $133,571 of a year’s $230,514, leaving about $96,943 a year to Lunenburg (our arithmetic).
